about: remote_view.answer_parts(text, lang) after the fix: a remote agent's final answer, credentials masked, with every markdown link, image, autolink, HTML anchor or image, reference definition and bare address shown as its words with its host in a code span, `words (`host`)` or, after Chinese words, `文字（`host`）`; an image as `🖼 alt`; a link with no host as its words; code (spans and fenced blocks) keeps its text, with a zero-width space after the colon of every `://` and inside every `](`, so nothing in it can be followed whether or not a client draws it as code; a NUL is dropped; an address with no host, and a mail address, in a code span whole; an address is read with any markdown escape in it taken out. `expected` is the list of messages. Generated from the Python worker (teams/teams_agent/answer_links.py); the TypeScript port must give the same. A backtick of the agent's own left in prose (one that opens no code span the rich text reads within a line) is shown as `ˋ`, so a code span made here pairs with nothing else; a mail address inside an address already made code is not made code again. Table rows (a line with a | over a separator line, and the rows after it that hold one) are read cell by cell, as the chat's rich text reads them. A bare domain is an address too: a run of labels (a dot or a hyphen possibly escaped) not right after an ASCII letter or digit, `.`, `-`, `@` or `/`, whose last label is any of two letters or more when it has three labels or more or a port, path, query or fragment after it, and a common generic top-level domain when it is `name.tld` alone (`README.md`, `self.id` stay words); it is shown whole, as the client shows it, in a code span (`main.py:42`).
